source_registry.title: Explicit Bounds for Primes in Arithmetic Progressions
source_registry.reason: For q>10^5 the sufficient cutoff contains exp(0.03*sqrt(q)*log(q)^3), which eventually exceeds u on the boundary q=u^(1/160).

source_registry.title: Medium-sized values for the Prime Number Theorem for primes in arithmetic progressions
source_registry.reason: The modulus is q<=log(x)^alpha1, with alpha1<2 in the fully explicit exceptional-zero-free statement.

source_registry.title: Explicit formulae for primes in arithmetic progressions, II
source_registry.reason: The result is an explicit Bombieri-Vinogradov-type sum over moduli, not the required pointwise lower bound for each q and a.

source_registry.title: Explicit zero-free regions for Dirichlet L-functions
source_registry.reason: The explicit R=5.60 result is restricted to 3<=q<=400000.

source_registry.title: Refinements to the Prime Number Theorem for Arithmetic Progressions
source_registry.reason: The range is structurally strong enough, but the relevant implied multiplier and decay constant are only effectively computable, not numerical.

source_registry.title: An Explicit Version of Bombieri's Log-Free Density Estimate and Sarkozy's Theorem for Shifted Primes
source_registry.reason: This is a zero-density estimate rather than the required pointwise prime-count theorem; the large prefactors and transfer cutoff must still be propagated.

source_registry.title: Explicit Deuring-Heilbronn phenomenon for Dirichlet L-functions
source_registry.reason: The effective corollary makes zero repulsion explicit but does not itself give a pointwise PNT-in-AP lower bound or common PAP cutoff.
